solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After Sabbath first stop for Scots lawyer

indicators.note: after says the ordinal comes behind the Sabbath letter in the answer

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for Sunday, the Christian Sabbath
first is written 1ST, and the figure 1 stands as the letter I

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer pausing proceedings right after the Sunday break.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'first stop' together, but 'first' is 1ST written with I for 1, placed 'After' the S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law the verb means to stay or halt a legal process, so a lawyer north of the border would use it for stop.

clue.text: Picnic food for Delia. Whisky's mine

parts.note: Scotch is whisky; the 's is a link meaning 'is'
egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine

explanation.surface: Delia Smith, the television cook, is told the whisky is the speaker's own.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook. 'mine' looks like a possessive, but it is the explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat and breadcrumbs is a standard British picnic snack.

clue.text: Measure of radiation dose it absorbs always when sun is overhead

indicators.note: in a down clue being overhead means standing above, so this letter comes first
absorbs means takes in, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: Radiation dose absorbed whenever the sun beats down from overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is overhead' works only in a down entry, where the S sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of equivalent radiation dose is named after the Swedish physicist Rolf Sievert.

clue.text: Triple crown: originally the internationally acclaimed rugby award

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: The rugby Triple Crown, an award won by beating the other three home nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triple crown' looks like the rugby honour named later; it is really the Pope's three-tiered headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal headdress is a crown of three tiers, often called the triple crown.

clue.text: In dry area I'll look for upturn with network of bars

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the whole thing from the bottom up
in places the contraction inside the dry area

parts.note: a desert is an arid area
the contraction written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone in a dry region hoping for a turn for the better, behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places the contraction inside the dry area, giving DESILLERT; 'look for upturn' reads that from the bottom up, which works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of crossed bars, so a structure fitted with one has a network of bars.

clue.text: Saxe blue turned gold on line that describes cloning

indicators.note: blue can mean upset or disordered, signalling that the letters are rearranged
turned means flipped round, so the chemical symbol is read backwards

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A Saxe blue fabric dyed gold, with a line on the label about cloning.
explanation.walkthrough: Saxe blue is a light greyish blue, but 'blue' is the anagram signal on SAXE, giving ASEX; 'turned' flips AU to UA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloning reproduces an organism without sex, which the adjective names.

clue.text: Makes 'oly sounds as means of catharsis

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to make holy is to hallow, and the dropped H of the 'oly gives 'allows

explanation.surface: A Cockney priest making holy noises as part of a cleansing ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in ''oly' tells you to drop the H of the synonym too: HALLOWS becomes 'ALLOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter plant drug was a classic purgative, and catharsis is purging.

clue.text: One who may pass exam sits when others leave

indicators.note: keeping some letters while the others go means taking every other letter, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A student sits an exam, ready to pass once the rest have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests an exam; it is a bridge call, and the player named after a compass point may make it.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, and any of them may pass in the bidding.

clue.text: Glory of drama we directed about — glory!

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled letters surround the exclamation
a drama that is directed is staged and arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise like 'Glory!'

explanation.surface: A drama we directed has brought us glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directed' gives EMAWARD and 'about' wraps it round the exclamation. 'Glory' appears twice: first as the definition, then as the cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning the American television prize brings glory to a programme and its makers.

clue.text: A ring's a place to deliver a punch

indicators.note: to place is to arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A boxing ring is the place to land a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' is the blow suggested by 'ring', but it is a drink; the apostrophe S counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish wine drink mixed with fruit is a kind of punch served in a bowl.

clue.text: Do men ever love PT, working out, bodybuilding?

indicators.note: working out suggests exercise but signals that the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: PT is physical training, taken here as its two letters

explanation.surface: Do men really love gym sessions and bodybuilding?
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like gym talk, which suits the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodybuilding taken to excess builds muscles beyond the normal, which is excessive growth of the body.

clue.text: Sebastian and Valentine are contemporary

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic middle-distance runner
Val is the short form of Valentine

explanation.surface: Two men, Sebastian and Valentine, said to be of the same generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of the same age or period as another is a contemporary of theirs.

clue.text: Mentally unbalanced puts on airs

indicators.note: on in a charade means joined to, so the second word follows the rearranged one
unbalanced means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mentally unbalanced puts on airs and graces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mentally unbalanced' reads as one phrase, but 'Mentally' alone is the definition, and only 'puts' is mixed up by 'unbalanced'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, the head is where the mind lives, so something going on there happens in the mind.

clue.text: New steel or plastic for mezzanine

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Choosing new steel or plastic as building material for a mezzanine floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' reads as a material beside steel, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word is a low storey between ground and first floors, the same as a mezzanine.

clue.text: Tote rules controlled roller tools

indicators.note: controlled means managed or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Betting rules for the Tote, the British racecourse betting operator, are regulated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tote is the British pool-betting operator, which primes 'roulette' as the wheel game, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers and dressmakers use small toothed wheels on handles to mark dots or perforations.

clue.text: Cossack general's right behind one setting cap

definitions.meaning: a hetman, the elected leader of a Cossack host
the phrase follows right behind setting one's cap

explanation.surface: A Cossack commander standing directly behind someone who is putting on a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: in the idiom, 'at a man' comes right after 'set one's cap', so three words sit right behind one setting cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian title was given to the elected military leader of a Cossack community.

clue.text: A European group assembled for court in Acts

definitions.text: A European group assembled for court in Acts

indicators.note: in places the assembled letters inside what is left of the book's name
for means in place of, so the abbreviation for court is taken out to make room
assembled means put together, so these letters are arranged

explanation.surface: An assembly of Europeans meeting as the court mentioned in the book of Acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' takes the court abbreviation out of the book's name and 'in' puts REOPAGU (the letters 'assembled') there. Read whole, the clue also describes the court where Paul spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian council on Mars Hill was a court; Paul spoke before it in Acts 17.

clue.text: Time to tuck in to well-cooked big lunch? Not here

definitions.text: Time to tuck in to well-cooked big lunch? Not here

indicators.note: tucking in means putting inside, so the letter goes into the scrambled meal
well-cooked means thoroughly stirred, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Time to sit down to a hearty lunch, though not at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-cooked' mixes the meal's letters and 'to tuck in to' puts the time letter inside. Read whole, the clue says this is no place for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-night venue for dancing and drinks does not serve lunch, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Eighteen holes at the capital of golf. St Andrew's?

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening capital letter

parts.note: a full round of golf is eighteen holes

explanation.surface: Playing eighteen holes at St Andrews, the so-called home of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews is the Scottish town famous for golf, but the apostrophe makes St Andrew's a sports venue, Birmingham City's football stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports stadium is a ground, and St Andrew's is the name of one, with the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Rabbie's first with a verse about robbers

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the poet's name
about means around in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Robert Burns, known as Rabbie, writing a poem about robbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbie is Robert Burns, the Scottish poet; the old Scots word for raiders suits him.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaving is raiding and plundering, so these raiders were robbers, especially on the Scottish border.

clue.text: Topsy-turvification jumbled not quite genuine pennies, old and new

indicators.note: jumbled means mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order
not quite drops the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: D was the old pre-decimal penny symbol, from Latin denarius
P is the new, decimal penny

explanation.surface: Turning everything upside down: a jumbled heap of fake coins, old and new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims GENUINE to GENUIN; with D and P these letters are 'jumbled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning something topsy-turvy is turning it on its head, a playful coinage for the act.

clue.text: So Jeddart justice victims were to swing under it

indicators.note: to swing is to move about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Victims of rough Border justice were hanged with the gallows over them.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeddart (Jedburgh) justice meant hanging first and trying afterwards, so its victims went to the gallows before any trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanged before any hearing, the victims had never been tried in court.

clue.text: Epiphany is night for tidying up

indicators.note: tidying up puts things into order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Twelfth Night, the Epiphany, is the night for tidying away the Christmas decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epiphany' points to the January feast; it means a sudden moment of understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden flash of understanding, a revelation, is an epiphany in everyday speech.

clue.text: Best name perhaps for servants' quarters

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Choosing the best name for the servants' living area.
explanation.definitionFit: In a grand house the staff lived and worked below stairs, in the lowest storey.

clue.text: Methuselah's father admits pressure to drop name for age

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the new letter enters the patriarch's name
to drop says the letter for name is taken out to make room

parts.note: in Genesis, Enoch is the father of Methuselah

explanation.surface: Methuselah's father, under pressure, giving up his name in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the Bible's oldest man, which primes 'age' as old age; it means an era.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a long, distinct period of history.

clue.text: Mud in your eye? Spatter or spit

indicators.note: to spatter is to scatter in drops, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Mud flying into your eye, from a splash or someone spitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mud in your eye' sounds like dirt; it is an old drinking toast, which the German-Latin toast matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts said when raising a glass: the Latin-derived one means may it do you good.

clue.text: Source of poison spread by Tory gang in Leeds

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are dispersed

explanation.surface: A poisonous influence spread by a Conservative gang in Leeds, the Yorkshire city.
explanation.definitionFit: This white Amanita mushroom is one of the most deadly fungi, so it is a source of toxin.

clue.text: Associate with MI6 without modification

parts.note: MI6 is also called SIS, the Secret Intelligence Service

explanation.surface: An associate working with British intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the existing state, with nothing changed.

clue.text: Vergil's art first grasped the meaning of the underworld

indicators.note: first puts the word for grasped ahead of the Latin verb

parts.note: to have grasped something is to have had hold of it
es is Latin for 'thou art' (sum, es, est), the language of the poet Vergil

explanation.surface: Studying Virgil's poetry, which first revealed what the underworld meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Vergil is the Latin poet, so 'art' is the Latin verb, not artistry; Book VI of his Aeneid is set in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god's name became the name of his realm, the abode of the dead.

clue.text: But's otherwise butt

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A quibble about wording: a 'but' read another way becomes 'butt'.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of a smoked cigarette is called either word, a leftover remnant.
